## Summary

itel is a phone brand established in 2007 that belongs to Transsion Holdings, with a registered office in the New Territories, Hong Kong and operational headquarters in Shenzhen; its products are sold mainly in emerging markets in Africa, South and Southeast Asia and Latin America [1]. Transsion, founded in Hong Kong in 2006 and based in Shenzhen, runs the TECNO, itel and Infinix phone brands [3]. itel's site lists S, P, CITY and A series phones, VistaTab tablets, smart watches, audio, and home appliances including TVs [4]. The IEEE registry lists 64 MA-L blocks and one MA-M block to "ITEL MOBILE LIMITED" at a Yau Tong, Kowloon, Hong Kong address [2][5].

A MAC in an itel block is most likely a low-cost itel phone or tablet [1][2][4]. Upstream's Secure-D, which found Triada and xHelper preinstalled on TECNO W2 phones in 2020, reported no signs of the malware on other Transsion models including itel [6], so security notes are empty. Radios, silicon and randomization are unknown: no itel specification page or teardown was reachable from the session that wrote this entry, and the FCC ID databases refused automated access; nothing is filled in from memory.
